recent_articles.title: Bolivia in crisis: Social unrest, demands for president to resign escalate | Protests News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rodrigo Paz**, Bolivia's president, is facing growing social unrest and demands for his resignation.  The protests began over a convergence of sector-based demands, including wage increases, contaminated fuel issues, and land classification changes. **Indigenous groups** from the highlands escalated the protests by blocking roads, demanding the president step down. Former President **Evo Morales**, who was ousted in 2019, has mobilized his supporters to pressure **President Paz**. The government is attempting to address legitimate demands while also cracking down on those deemed hostile to democracy.  The unrest has led to violence and clashes between protesters and police, with over 120 people detained.  **Jose Luis Lupo**, the Presidency Minister, stated that the government will use dialogue for legitimate sectors and full force of the law against those attacking democracy. The situation remains fluid as authorities seek a path forward.

recent_articles.title: Danny Go: YouTube star Danny Go mourns heartbreaking loss of 14-year-old son Isaac - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Danny Go**, a popular YouTuber known for his family-friendly show "Danny Go!", announced the death of his 14-year-old son, Isaac, who had been battling stage 3 mouth cancer since late 2025.  **Go** shared a heartfelt tribute on Instagram, expressing his immense love and pride in his son's strength despite facing health challenges. Fans and fellow creators have expressed condolences and support for the family during this difficult time. **Go** canceled his tour to focus on supporting Isaac and creating special memories with him.

recent_articles.title: PTI workers stage protests in various cities, defy Section 144 in Islamabad - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **PTI** and **TTAP** organized protests across Pakistan on Friday, demanding the release of former prime minister Imran Khan and addressing concerns over inflation, rising petroleum prices, and deteriorating law and order.  **PTI Islamabad President Aamir Mughal**, along with other leaders, held a protest in Islamabad despite Section 144 being in place, while **Shandana Gulzar** from **TTAP** spoke at a press conference in Peshawar, highlighting the plight of civilians in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and accusing the federal government of mismanagement. These protests were joined by political and social activists across the country, including those from the Haqooq-i-Khalq Party.

recent_articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists allege abuse by Israeli forces while detained
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Canadian** Foreign Minister Anita Anand confirmed that her officials have received information detailing the "appalling abuse" of Canadian citizens detained in Israel following the interception of a Gaza-bound aid flotilla. **Germany** and **Spain** also reported injuries among their nationals, while organizers of the Global Sumud Flotilla alleged at least 15 cases of sexual assaults and other mistreatment.  The **Israeli** prison service dismissed the allegations as false, stating all detainees were held in accordance with the law.

recent_articles.title: Tulsi Gabbard resigns as US director of national intelligence
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tulsi Gabbard**, the US director of national intelligence under **President Donald Trump**, will resign from her position on June 30th.  She cited her husband's recent bone cancer diagnosis as the reason for her departure, stating she cannot continue in her role while he faces this challenge. **Trump** expressed his support for Gabbard and noted her "incredible job" during her tenure.  **Aaron Lukas**, the principal deputy director, will assume the acting director position.

recent_articles.title: Why is the US putting pressure on Cuba and what are Trump's aims?
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The United States is escalating pressure on Cuba, accusing the country of posing a national security threat and recently indicting former leader Raúl Castro. The US has imposed an oil blockade, sanctions, and a murder indictment against Castro, citing an incident in 1996 where Cuban fighter jets shot down two civilian planes owned by Cuban exiles.  Cuba maintains its actions were justified as self-defense within its airspace and accuses the US of using the charges to justify military aggression. The US has also targeted senior Cuban officials accused of human rights abuses or corruption, while offering $100 million in aid through humanitarian organizations. Cuba's response has been characterized by fiery rhetoric, with leaders demanding an end to the blockade and accusing the US of "coercion" and threats. China and Russia have condemned the US pressure on Cuba.

recent_articles.title: State-sponsored apprenticeships and decriminalising cannabis on the bill at Victoria’s Labor conference | Jacinta Allan | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Jacinta Allan**, Victorian Premier, will announce a plan to create a government-owned electricity body that will hire electrical apprentices at the Labor party's final state conference before the election. The plan aims to address workforce shortages in the industry and is inspired by her father's experience as a linesman at the **State Electricity Commission** (SEC).  The conference will also feature discussions on various policy proposals, including reducing workweeks, increasing reproductive health leave, decriminalizing cannabis, and addressing issues like public transport affordability.

recent_articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists allege sexual assault and rape in Israeli detention | Israel | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Activists** released from **Israeli** custody following their detention on a flotilla attempting to deliver aid to Gaza have alleged abuse, including sexual assaults and injuries.  **Israel’s** prison service denies the allegations, stating all detainees are treated in accordance with the law and medical care is provided according to professional judgment. Several countries, including **Germany**, **Italy**, and **France**, reported injuries and accusations of serious misconduct, prompting investigations into possible crimes like kidnapping and sexual assault.  The incident has further strained relations between Israel and international organizations and governments.

recent_articles.title: Bowring Hospital wall collapse: Lokayukta probe finds major safety lapses - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A **Lokayukta** inquiry into the fatal wall collapse at the **Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital** in Shivajinagar, Karnataka, has revealed multiple structural and administrative failures. The investigation found that the wall was constructed beyond permissible height limits, had been damaged previously, and lacked proper drainage systems and retaining walls.  The inquiry also highlighted negligence by authorities who failed to monitor dangerous structures and encroachments. **Senior IAS and IPS officers**, officials from various departments, and hospital authorities appeared before the **Lokayukta** for questioning. The **Lokayukta** directed authorities to identify similar unsafe structures and take preventive measures.

recent_articles.title: Ebola risk now at highest level in DR Congo, says WHO - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The World Health Organisation (WHO)** has raised the risk assessment level for the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo to very high, citing a rapidly spreading epidemic with nearly 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths.  **Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus**, **WHO** chief, emphasized the urgency of containing the virus, particularly due to violence and insecurity hindering response efforts. While Uganda's situation is stable, **WHO** has deployed international staff and prioritized existing treatments like monoclonal antibodies and olibdesivir for clinical trials.

recent_articles.title: Nascar legend Kyle Busch dies aged 41
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kyle Busch**, a two-time Nascar Cup Series champion, died at age 41. The **Busch family**, **Richard Childress Racing**, and **Nascar** announced the sudden passing of the racing legend who was ninth on the circuit's all-time win list.  Tributes poured in from fellow drivers and organizations, including former teammate Denny Hamlin, Brad Keselowski, Speedway Motorsports, and Dale Earnhardt Jr., who remembered Busch as a "champion among champions" and a "once-in-a-generation competitor."

recent_articles.title: Soft power sell-off: anger as British Council announces sale of historic Madrid building | Foreign policy | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The British Council**, a global organization promoting understanding between the UK and other countries, is facing backlash from staff over proposed cuts and restructuring. **Staff in Spain** are protesting the sale of its Madrid headquarters, with concerns about job security and leadership decisions. The organization is struggling to pay off a £197 million debt incurred during the Covid-era, prompting drastic measures including potential sales of buildings in other European countries.  The British Council maintains it remains committed to its mission but acknowledges the financial challenges and is taking steps to ensure its long-term sustainability.

recent_articles.title: WHO says 12th person infected with hantavirus detected in the Netherlands | Health News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **World Health Organization (WHO)** confirmed a 12th hantavirus case in the Netherlands, involving a Dutch crew member on the MV Hondius cruise ship.  **Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus**, WHO chief, urged countries to continue monitoring passengers and cautioned against further spread. The infected crew member is isolated at a hospital while over 600 contacts are being monitored in 30 countries. The **Dutch National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM)** stated that the chance of further spread remains low.

recent_articles.title: Renowned infectious diseases expert Dr Naseem Salahuddin passes away - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dr. Naseem Salahuddin**, a renowned infectious diseases expert and professor emeritus at **Indus Hospital**, passed away on Friday.  The hospital expressed its sorrow over her passing, noting her dedication to patient care, medical education, and humanitarian service. Dr. Salahuddin was a member of the World Health Organization’s Expert Advisory Panel on Rabies since 2004 and played a pivotal role in raising awareness about rabies prevention and treatment. She also authored books and contributed to various scholarly journals and news outlets including Dawn.

recent_articles.title: Tennessee execution called off after failed lethal injection
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A **Tennessee** execution of Tony Carruthers, convicted of kidnapping and murdering three people in 1994, was postponed after staff were unable to find a suitable vein for the lethal injection.  The **Department of Corrections** stated that while they found a primary IV line, they could not establish a backup line as required by protocol. Governor Bill Lee granted Carruthers a temporary reprieve from execution for one year. The **American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU)** and other advocates have raised concerns about the trial's integrity and called for DNA testing. Kim Kardashian also joined the cause, urging supporters to demand the evidence be tested before it's too late.

recent_articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists allege abuse, sexual assault in Israeli detention | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera

The **Israeli** prison service denies the allegations, stating that all detainees are held according to the law with full regard for their basic rights.

recent_articles.title: Suspected Ebola cases triple in a week as WHO warns of rapid spread in DRC | Global development | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The World Health Organization (WHO)** has revised its threat assessment for the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo to "very high," citing a rapid spread and increasing number of suspected cases. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, is concentrated in Ituri province with some cases reported elsewhere in the country and neighboring Uganda. **Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus**, WHO director-general, highlighted the need to address distrust among local communities for successful response efforts while acknowledging a "good sign" of improved detection rates.  Despite these challenges, **Dr Anne Ancia**, WHO representative in the DRC, remains optimistic about containing the outbreak.

recent_articles.title: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto inaugurates 39km-long Shahrah-i-Bhutto linking Qayyumabad to M9 Motorway - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari** inaugurated the 39-kilometer Shahrah-i-Bhutto Expressway, linking Karachi's Qayyumabad to the M-9 Motorway.  He also laid the foundation stone for a new expressway project connecting Karachi Port to Qayyumabad. **Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah** highlighted the expressway's six interchanges, lanes, and elevated section, emphasizing its potential to reduce travel time by an hour. **Bilawal Bhutto Zardari** emphasized the PPP's commitment to public-private partnerships in developing Karachi and Pakistan, citing projects worth billions of rupees underway. He also announced plans for a Sindh International Financial Centre and a defense production zone in Karachi.

recent_articles.title: UK scientists developing Ebola vaccine that could be ready for trials in months
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Oxford University** scientists are developing a new Ebola vaccine using the same technology employed during the COVID-19 pandemic. The experimental vaccine, which uses a modified chimpanzee cold virus to deliver genetic material about the Bundibugyo species of Ebola virus, could be ready for clinical trials in two to three months. **The World Health Organization (WHO)** has upgraded the risk level from "high" to "very high" in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where the outbreak is centered. The vaccine will likely be used through ring vaccination, targeting those most at risk of infection and close contacts of infected individuals.

recent_articles.title: Ebola risk raised to 'very high' in DR Congo
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **World Health Organization (WHO)** has raised the Ebola risk in the Democratic Republic of Congo to "very high" due to the outbreak's rapid spread and fatality rate.  **Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus**, WHO head, stated that while the risk is high in the region and globally, it remains low at a global level. The outbreak has resulted in 177 suspected deaths and 750 suspected cases so far, with no proven vaccine for the rare Bundibugyo strain.  Scientists are developing new vaccines, but their effectiveness remains uncertain.

recent_articles.title: Man City confirm Guardiola exit to end decade-long, trophy-laden spell | Football News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pep Guardiola** is stepping down as **Manchester City** manager after a decade in charge, bringing an end to one of the most successful eras in English football.  He leaves with 20 trophies won, including six Premier League titles and the Champions League. Guardiola's departure follows a disappointing season where City finished second in the league, despite winning the domestic cup double this season. He will be succeeded by his former assistant, **Mikel Arteta**.

recent_articles.title: Trump’s ‘disappointment’ with Nato lays groundwork for ‘one of the most important’ summits ever, Rubio says – Europe live | World news | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming NATO summit in Ankara will address **Trump**'s disappointment with the alliance's response to US operations in the Middle East.  **Rutte**, **Malmer Stenergard**, and other officials emphasized the need for increased defense spending, industrial capacity building, and a stronger commitment to Article 5.  Meanwhile, protests erupted against the new US consulate opening in Greenland after comments by the special envoy suggesting a return of US influence on the territory. The summit also saw discussions about Iran's nuclear program and efforts to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

recent_articles.title: How a failed attempt to protect a tablecloth led to Jacques E. Brandenberger’s invention of “cellophane” | - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Jacques E. Brandenberger**, a Swiss inventor born in 1872, accidentally discovered **Cellophane** while trying to create stain-resistant fabric.  Inspired by observing wine being spilled on a tablecloth, he developed a flexible cellulose film that became widely used in food packaging and consumer goods due to its transparency and protective qualities. The invention revolutionized retail packing, offering consumers the ability to view products before purchase, and paved the way for modern transparent packaging. **Cellophane**, while initially intended for textiles, has become a symbol of modernity and hygiene, with its biodegradability making it an attractive alternative to single-use plastics in today's market.

recent_articles.title: Iran’s enriched uranium stockpile: Can it be safely transferred? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **President Donald Trump** reiterated that the US will not allow Iran to keep its enriched uranium stockpile, while **Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei** issued a directive prohibiting the removal of the uranium from Iranian soil.  The future of the estimated 440kg of highly enriched uranium remains a sticking point in peace negotiations between the US and Iran. While experts say it is possible to transfer enriched uranium safely, concerns remain about its potential for misuse. The **International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)** has specific protocols for transporting enriched uranium hexafluoride, but the issue of transferring this material safely from Iran remains unresolved.

recent_articles.title: RO systems should be maintained properly to be effective, says study - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A recent study in Chennai, India, found that while **reverse osmosis (RO)** systems effectively remove microbes under ideal conditions, they are not a guarantee for safe drinking water. The study, published in the Journal of Exposure Science & Environmental Epidemiology, revealed that 31% of post-RO samples still contained **Escherichia coli** (E. coli), compared to 71% in untreated water.  The researchers found a correlation between education level and E. coli contamination, with higher levels of education associated with lower rates of contamination. The study emphasizes the need for proper maintenance and hygiene practices alongside reliable piped water supply and affordable servicing structures to ensure safe drinking water access.

recent_articles.title: IHC bans killing of stray dogs, orders authorities to implement humane methods of population control - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Islamabad High Court (IHC)** has banned the killing of stray dogs in the federal capital, ordering authorities to implement a humane population control program. The court ruled that mass killing of animals is not consistent with Islamic law or international principles and directed the Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad, the Capital Development Authority (CDA), and other relevant bodies to ensure no inhumane actions are taken against stray dogs.  The court also ordered the creation of an advisory committee, a dog bite database, and improved waste management in residential and commercial areas.

recent_articles.title: PM Shehbaz says Pakistan taking measures on a priority basis to increase foreign investment - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif** met with a delegation from **Qatar’s Taameer Group**, led by its founder **Mohammad Al Ali**.  The meeting focused on increasing foreign investment in Pakistan, with **Sharif** highlighting the removal of obstacles hindering investment and emphasizing Pakistan's potential in sectors like tourism, hospitality, real estate, and construction. The **Taameer Group** expressed interest in investing in these areas and has already begun work on several projects.

recent_articles.title: Africa summit in India postponed over Ebola outbreak fears
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **India-Africa Forum Summit**, scheduled for May 28-31 in Delhi, has been postponed due to the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. The **World Health Organization** declared the latest outbreak a public health emergency of international concern, with over 600 suspected cases and 139 deaths reported so far.  The postponement was announced jointly by **India** and the **African Union**, citing the "emerging public health situation in the continent."

recent_articles.title: Amazon Uk Chief: ‘It’s not their fault’: Amazon UK boss says education system is failing young workers | World News - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amazon’s UK country manager, John Boumphrey**, argued that the education system is failing to prepare young people for work, contributing to rising unemployment. He stated that businesses are struggling to recruit workers with the necessary skills despite a million young people being out of education, employment or training. **Boumphrey** called for work experience placements to become compulsory and closer cooperation between businesses, local authorities and further education colleges to address regional skills shortages.  He emphasized that Amazon is facing difficulty recruiting enough workers for technical and engineering roles due to automation and robotics expansion in its warehouses.

recent_articles.title: Babar, Naseem recalled as PCB announces 16-member squad for Australia ODIs - Sport - DAWN.COM

The team will assemble in Islamabad on Friday and begin training on Saturday, with the Australian team arriving in Islamabad on Saturday as well.

recent_articles.title: States should be allowed to conduct CET for medical courses: CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** called for the decentralization of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) and urged **States** to have the opportunity to conduct their own Common Entrance Tests (CET) for medical courses. He argued that education is a concurrent list subject, allowing states to independently administer entrance exams for professional courses within the federal system.

recent_articles.title: Melanoma skin cancer cases in UK hit record level, analysis finds | Skin cancer | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Cancer Research UK** has reported a record high of 20,980 melanoma cases in the UK for 2022, with projections suggesting that by 2040 there could be 26,500 new cases annually. The charity attributes the increase to the UK's growing and ageing population, and emphasizes that most cases are preventable through sun safety measures like seeking shade, covering up, and using sunscreen. **Fiona Osgun**, head of health information at **Cancer Research UK**, advises protecting skin from UV damage even on cooler or cloudier days. **Prof Peter Johnson**, national clinical director for cancer at **NHS England**, stresses the importance of sensible sun exposure practices to prevent melanoma, urging individuals to seek medical attention if they notice any unusual changes in their skin.

recent_articles.title: Calcutta HC orders setting up SIT of CBI to probe hushing up charges in R G Kar rape-murder case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Calcutta High Court** ordered the creation of a three-member special investigation team (SIT) from the **CBI** to investigate the death of a trainee doctor at the **RG Kar Medical College and Hospital**. The court's decision follows allegations that evidence was destroyed and attempts were made to downplay the incident. The SIT will focus on the events leading up to the victim's cremation, including potential lapses in the initial investigation by both police and hospital authorities.  The team is expected to file a comprehensive report by June 25th.

recent_articles.title: Tennessee governor orders stay of execution after doctor can’t find vein | US news | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Governor Bill Lee** of Tennessee granted a one-year stay of execution for Tony Carruthers, who was scheduled to be executed on Thursday.  Carruthers's lawyers argued that he is mentally incompetent and there was a lack of physical evidence linking him to the 1994 murders. The reprieve came after Carruthers's legal team filed a last-minute appeal citing difficulties locating his vein during the lethal injection attempt, as well as concerns about the physician contracted by Tennessee’s department of corrections.  Carruthers's case has drawn attention due to ongoing questions about his conviction and mental competency, as well as protests against his execution.

recent_articles.title: Kyle Busch, two-time Nascar champion, dies aged 41 | US news | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kyle Busch**, a two-time Nascar Cup Series champion, has died at the age of 41.  The racing organization announced his passing on Thursday, expressing condolences to his family and the motorsports community. **Busch** had been hospitalized with a severe illness earlier in the day, and was unable to compete in this weekend's race in Charlotte, North Carolina. He won championships in 2015 and 2019 and is survived by his wife Samantha and children Brexton and Lennix.

recent_articles.title: Single-sex toilets must exclude transgender people, says EHRC | Gender | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC)** has released a new code of practice for public bodies, businesses, and service providers in England, Wales, and Scotland regarding single-sex facilities. The guidance clarifies that while services must adhere to the supreme court's ruling on sex in the Equality Act 2010, they can offer alternative options like gender-neutral toilets for those who do not wish to use services based on their biological sex.  The document acknowledges potential negative impacts on transgender individuals and encourages a broader conversation about inclusive access to facilities. However, it also emphasizes that excluding trans people from single-sex facilities is not proportionate in healthcare settings where mixed-sex accommodation is unavailable. The code remains in draft form and will be finalized after 40 days of parliamentary review.

recent_articles.title: Air France and Airbus held guilty over deadly 2009 Atlantic flight disaster - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Air France** and **Airbus** were found guilty of manslaughter by a Paris appeals court for their role in the 2009 crash of Air France Flight 447, which killed all 228 people on board. The court ruled that the companies bore responsibility for the crash, overturning an earlier decision that had cleared them of criminal liability. Both companies were fined €225,000 each and plan to appeal the verdict.  The families of the victims expressed disappointment with the sentence, but **Daniele Lamy**, president of the AF447 victims’ association, welcomed the ruling as a step towards accountability for the tragedy.

recent_articles.title: New govt. hospital, preventing waterlogging are among my priorities, says Katpadi MLA - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Who is Mohammed Omar, $90-million fraud suspect in Minnesota, who jumped from balcony to evade FBI arrest? - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mohammed Omar**, charged with conspiracy to commit health care fraud and four counts of health care fraud, jumped from a fourth-floor balcony during an FBI arrest attempt in Minnesota on Thursday. **Colin McDonald**, Assistant Attorney General for the National Fraud Enforcement Division, urged the public to help capture Omar, who allegedly operated two companies, North Home Health Care and South Home Health Care, with Ibrahim Bashir Abdi to defraud the government of $90 million through falsified service hours. recent_articles.title: UK launches ‘Great British Summer Savings’ to ease family costs | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera

recent_articles.title: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: Angry crowd sets Rwampara hospital tents on fire

The **World Health Organization (WHO)** has declared it a "public health emergency of international concern," but not at pandemic level.  The outbreak, caused by a rare species of Ebola known as Bundibugyo, has resulted in 139 deaths and two cases in neighboring Uganda.

recent_articles.title: News live: Australian flotilla activists released by Israel arrive in Istanbul and claim they were denied food and water | Australia news | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dr Hillel Newman**, Israel's ambassador to Australia, stated that no one from the 400+ people detained on the Global Sumud Flotilla was harmed. **Newman** also claimed that the interception of the flotilla was done with "great sensitivity" by Israeli security forces. recent_articles.title: India's 'Cockroach Janta Party' goes viral, spotlights Gen Z worries - World - DAWN.COM

The CJP, founded by 30-year-old Abhijeet Dipke, addresses issues like unemployment, inflation, and political representation, resonating with a large segment of young Indians who feel ignored by mainstream politics. Dipke emphasizes the CJP's commitment to democratic and peaceful means of political engagement, while also acknowledging its potential for significant change within Indian politics.

recent_articles.title: Qatar-based British-Pakistani scientist develops AI eye scan for early dementia diagnosis - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Professor Rayaz Malik**, a British-Pakistani scientist based in Qatar, has developed an AI-powered eye scan using corneal confocal microscopy (CCM) that can detect dementia and diabetic nerve damage years before symptoms appear.  This technology, traditionally used to diagnose infections and abnormalities in the front surface of the eye, has been shown to identify microscopic nerve fibre damage associated with diseases such as diabetes, chemotherapy, inflammatory disorders, and infectious diseases. **Professor Malik** believes this could be particularly important for countries facing ageing populations and rising rates of neurological disease.  The technology's ability to detect early-stage cognitive decline could lead to more effective treatments and earlier interventions.

recent_articles.title: Bihar midday meal incident: HC asks whether NGO can continue providing meals - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Ebola tensions rise as treatment centre torched in DR Congo’s Ituri | Ebola News | Al Jazeera

recent_articles.title: Patient tests HIV-positive after surgery, triggering probe at Multan’s Nishtar Hospital - Pakistan - DAWN.COM

recent_articles.title: Body donated for educational purposes cannot be returned: Kerala HC - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Kerala High Court** ruled that a woman's body, donated to the **Government Medical College, Kalamassery**, cannot be returned based on her children's request. The court emphasized that the deceased's intention to donate her body for educational purposes overrides any subsequent requests from her children.  As a result, the court dismissed their plea seeking the return of their mother's remains.
